product.title: The League in a Box
product.summary: Design the rules of a league, then meet the league you designed.
product.whatStudentsDo: Students set nine governance levers — a spending cap, revenue sharing, a tax on high spenders, contract limits, draft order, rookie pay, expansion pace, player movement and enforcement — then ratify them. The engine profiles the league they built, names its character, and shows a matrix of who wins and who loses under those rules.
product.technology: single-file HTML build plus a React/Vite rewrite published from docs/

studentDataProfile.notes: State kept in browser localStorage only; no server call observed.

governance.maturityBasis: Complete and reachable in two implementations, with a committed build output. No student-run evidence exists.

health.technicalBasis: Playtested end to end 2026-08-16. Ten policy levers produce genuinely different league typologies with a stakeholder matrix that rewrites its wording, not just its numbers. Deterministic, and the most conceptually ambitious design in the account.
knownBlockers: Written far above its stated audience: "stochastic allocation", "progressive spending penalties", "interclub revenue redistribution", "typology", "oligopoly". This is aimed at grades 5 to 8.
No scarcity anywhere — the ten levers are independent with no shared budget, so nothing stops a student maxing every dial in one direction and there is no tradeoff pressure while deciding.
No score, no win state and nothing to regret, so there is no reason to replay it.
On a phone the option labels look tappable but are not; only the small range-input thumb responds, which is a poor touch target for a three-position control.

governance.notes: Its own copy calls it a Track 101 capstone, so it is filed under Track 101 rather than as an unattached standalone — but it appears in no Track 101 lesson list. Worth reconciling against the curriculum.

curation.tierBasis: The most ambitious concept in the account — design a league and see who benefits — with nothing scarce, no score, and copy written for policy analysts rather than the grades 5 to 8 it targets.

provenance.evidence: league-in-a-box/src/league-in-a-box-advanced.jsx labels the intro screen 'Track 101 Capstone' and closes with 'Check out BOW Sports Capital's Track 101 to understand league governance.' Recorded as one experience across two implementations.
